ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: (2017·Nanjing Third Mock Exam) As shown in Figure 11, in the electric field of point charge -q, there is placed an insulating rectangular thin plate carrying a certain amount of charge with uniformly distributed charge, MN is its axis of symmetry, and point O is the geometric center. The distances between point charge -q and a, O, b are respectively d, 2d, 3d. It is known that the electric field strength at point a in the figure is zero, then what is the magnitude of the electric field strength produced by the charged thin plate at point b in the figure?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an insulating rectangular thin plate uniformly charged, with geometric center O, and the horizontal dashed line MN is the axis of symmetry. Point b is on the left side of the thin plate, point a is on the right side of the thin plate, and point charge −q is on the right side of point a. The distance labels below show that b to O is d, O to a is d, and a to −q is d, so taking O as the origin, one may take b=-d, a=+d, and point charge −q at +2d. Reasoning: Take horizontally to the right as the positive direction. At point a, the distance from a to the negative point charge −q is d, and the electric field produced by a negative charge points toward the negative charge, that is, to the right, so E_q(a)=+kq/d^2. It is known that the total electric field at point a is zero, therefore the electric field produced by the thin plate at point a must be E_plate(a)=-kq/d^2. Since the charge of the rectangular thin plate is uniformly distributed and centrally symmetric about O, a and b are symmetric about O, so the electric fields produced by the thin plate at these two points have equal magnitudes and opposite directions, that is, E_plate(b)=-E_plate(a)=+kq/d^2. Then look at the electric field of point charge −q at point b: the distance from b to −q is 3d, the direction is also to the right, and the magnitude is E_q(b)=kq/(3d)^2=kq/(9d^2). Therefore the magnitude of the electric field strength at point b is E_b=E_plate(b)+E_q(b)=kq/d^2+kq/(9d^2).
